caveats:
The product contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2023), processed by ESA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS), using the Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) system originally developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, and modified at EOS-RS.

This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the ALOS-2 satellite operated by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) before (11 Dec 2022) and during (14 May 2023) the event.

This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the ALOS-2 satellite operated by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) before (19 Feb 2023) and during (14 May 2023) the event.

These are preliminary maps derived from satellite radar and should be used as guidance only. Coloured pixels may include false positives, and their absence does not mean an absence of damage or flooding.
methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

# Myanmar Cyclone Mocha: Damage and Flood Proxy Maps, May 2023

The **Earth Observatory of Singapore – Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS)** produced these damage and flood proxy maps for Myanmar Cyclone Mocha (May 2023) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images. Each map is a separate ZIP below with its GeoTIFF, a KMZ for Google Earth, the PNG figures and a text file describing how it was made and how to read it.

## Maps in this dataset

- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Myanmar, Cyclone Mocha, 18 May 2023, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Myanmar, Cyclone Mocha, 18 May 2023, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Flood Proxy Map: Myanmar, Cyclone Mocha, 14 May 2023, v0.4**
- **EOS-RS Flood Proxy Map: Myanmar, Cyclone Mocha, 14 May 2023, v0.3** (superseded)

**More map details and files:** <https://sf.earthobservatory.sg/event/EOS-RS_202305_Myanmar_Cyclone_Mocha>

**More map details and files:** <http://eos-rs-products.earthobservatory.sg/EOS-RS_202305_Myanmar_Cyclone_Mocha/>

organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.

The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary Damage Proxy Map (DPM) depicting areas that are likely damaged in west Myanmar due to Cyclone Mocha which made landfall on 14 May 2023. This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellite operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) before (18 Jan 2023 to 6 May 2023) and after (18 May 2023) the event.
